notes:
Research notes for Toronto, Canada, as of Monday, October 12, 2026. No official, single "the" 5-year fixed rate exists. The figure depends on the lender and on whether the mortgage is insured (down payment under 20%) or uninsured.

- **Lowest rates:**
  - Several comparison sites carry dates of October 13, one day after `today`, and I can't explain that.
  - Ratehub lists the best high-ratio (insured) 5-year fixed rate in Canada at 4.34%.
  - Wowa gives the same 4.34% as the lowest insured 5-year fixed rate. It says this is 25 bps higher than 30 days ago and 14 bps higher than 7 days ago.
  - Wowa puts the lowest conventional (uninsurable) 5-year fixed rate at 4.44%. That is a different figure from Wowa's own later line quoting 4.64% for uninsurable mortgages, so its numbers don't agree with each other.
  - Ratehub's FAQ section said Scotiabank had the lowest Big 6 rate at 4.29% as of September 8, 2026. That is older and out of date.
- **Big banks:**
  - Ratehub's table (updated October 13) shows a Big 6 bank at 4.54% and Scotiabank at 4.74%.
  - Nesto says its own 4.59% compares with a Big 6 average of 5.17% on a 5-year fixed.
  - An earlier Nesto page (October 8) put the Big 6 average discounted conventional 5-year fixed at 5.14%.
  - BMO raised its standard 5-year fixed by 20 basis points to 5.14% on October 7.
  - BMO's high-ratio 5-year fixed rose to 4.99%.
- **Posted rates:** According to the Bank of Canada, the average 5-year posted rate at the major banks is 6.09%. This comes from a Forbes page that is about 56 days old. Posted rates are the banks' list prices, and borrowers usually get discounted rates instead.
- **Direction:**
  - Rates are climbing in October 2026, after all six of the largest banks raised select fixed rates since early September.
  - Fixed rates have risen since early September, while variable rates haven't moved.
- **Other context:** The Bank of Canada policy rate is 2.25%, held on September 2. The next Bank of Canada decision is October 28.
- **Gaps:**
  - The search results don't give a Toronto- or Ontario-specific rate.
  - I don't know whether the asker means an insured or uninsured mortgage, or a new purchase versus a renewal. That changes which figure applies.
